page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-8 is a flexible compute instance powered by the Ampere Altra processor family using the arm64 64-bit architecture. The configuration is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed base frequency of 3.0 GHz, supporting 1 thread per core to deliver 4 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading overhead. Memory capacity is allocated at 8.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

The hardware configuration includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and omits integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for operating systems and persistent data. Graphical processing units are not present. The dedicated single-threaded core design delivers consistent execution profiles by eliminating resource contention common to hyperthreaded architectures, though x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX and AMX instructions are absent on this platform.

With its 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, the VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-8 functions efficiently for compute-focused tasks that require dedicated processor cycles over massive in-memory storage. Primary workload targets include ARM-native software builds, CI/CD execution nodes, containerized microservices, web servers, and batch processing tasks tailored for aarch64 environments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-8 is an arm64-based compute instance built on the Ampere Altra processor line operating at 3.0 GHz. The setup features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU profile. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and does not integrate local storage or GPU hardware, depending instead on external block storage for data persistence. By dedicating entire physical cores to virtual cores without hyperthreading, it avoids sibling-thread contention and provides stable performance for processor-oriented jobs. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-8 is suited for native ARM compilation, CI/CD pipelines, container hosting, web servers, and distributed application workloads that do not demand extensive memory footprints.
